info.text: Unit 31 — Clarifying meaning in English as a lingua franca. CEFR B2. Items split by skill: Listening, Reading, Use of English, Vocabulary.

name.text: U31-L1 Dialogue 1 — what P12 identifies

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The line technician and the OEM engineer discuss the code P12. What does P12 identify?

generalfeedback.text: P12 is the whole connector; TP12 is one test pin inside it. That was the misunderstanding the two speakers cleared up.

feedback.text: No — the diagram is checked against the part number.
No — the readout is the message on the panel.

name.text: U31-L2 Dialogue 1 — making letters clear

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The two letters sound similar on the phone. How does the engineer make them clear?

generalfeedback.text: He spells the code in the phonetic alphabet — Tango, Papa, one, two. This makes P and T impossible to confuse.

answer.text: By repeating the whole task card aloud

feedback.text: No — he spells the code, not the task card.

answer.text: By speaking a little louder each time

feedback.text: Volume does not fix P versus T on a phone.

answer.text: By sending a brand new wiring diagram

feedback.text: No — that is not what he does here.

name.text: U31-L3 Dialogue 2 — meaning of TP12 open

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The BITE readout shows “TP12 open”. What does this mean?

generalfeedback.text: “Open” means the test pin currently has no connection. The fix is to reseat the connector and run the BITE test again.

answer.text: The test pin has no connection
The connector is now fitted correctly

feedback.text: No — open is a fault, not a pass.

answer.text: The task card reference is wrong

feedback.text: No — the readout is about the pin, not the card.

answer.text: The BITE test has fully passed

feedback.text: No — a passed test would not report open.

name.text: U31-L4 Dialogue 2 — register of the tech log

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The speakers agree that the tech log can stay casual, like the hangar talk.

True or false?

generalfeedback.text: False. They agree the conversation can be casual, but the written tech-log record must stay formal, accurate and clear.

feedback.text: Correct — the log stays formal even when the talk is casual.
No — only the talk is casual; the log is formal.

name.text: U31-L5 Dialogue 1 — the number in TP12

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The engineer spells the reference as Tango, Papa, one, two. Write the number in the reference TP12 as digits.

generalfeedback.text: “One, two” spoken together is the number 12. So the reference is TP12.

feedback.text: Both digits are spoken: one AND two = 12.

name.text: U31-L6 Dialogue 1 — how many test pins

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The engineer says TP12 is one individual test pin inside the connector. How many test pins does TP12 mean? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: TP12 is a single test pin — the number is 1. P12 is the connector that holds it.

name.text: U31-L7 Dialogue 1 — letters spelled before the digits

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Before the digits, the engineer spells the letters Tango and Papa. Write how many letters he spells.

generalfeedback.text: Tango (T) and Papa (P) are two letters. Then the digits one and two follow.

name.text: U31-R1 Work order — what the night shift found

questiontext.text:
Read this work-order handover note, then answer.

WORK ORDER — HANDOVER NOTE. Bay 3, A320, ATA 24. The night shift found a reference query on connector P12. The task card and the wiring diagram did not match. The technician called the OEM desk and confirmed the code. P12 is the connector. TP12 is the test pin inside it. Both codes were read back in the phonetic alphabet. Do not fit any connector until the reference is confirmed against the diagram.

What did the night shift find on connector P12?

generalfeedback.text: They found a reference query: the task card and the wiring diagram did not match.

feedback.text: No — the note reports a code query, not damage.
No — the card exists; it did not match the diagram.

name.text: U31-R2 Work order — card and diagram matched

questiontext.text:
Read the work-order note again. The task card and the wiring diagram matched each other.

True or false?

generalfeedback.text: False. The note says the task card and the wiring diagram did NOT match — that is why the technician called the OEM.

feedback.text: No — the note says they did not match.

name.text: U31-R3 Work order — what TP12 is

questiontext.text: Read the work-order note again. According to the note, what is TP12?

generalfeedback.text: The note states plainly: P12 is the connector, and TP12 is the test pin inside it.

answer.text: A test pin inside the connector
The connector that joins two wire sets
The message shown on the BITE panel
A code for the whole task card

feedback.text: No — TP12 names a pin, not the card.

name.text: U31-R4 Work order — codes read back phonetically

questiontext.text:
Read the work-order note again. Both codes were read back in the phonetic alphabet.

True or false?

generalfeedback.text: True. The note says both codes were read back in the phonetic alphabet, so P12 and TP12 could not be confused.

feedback.text: Correct — both codes were read back phonetically.
No — the note says both codes were read back.

name.text: U31-R5 Work order — when a connector may be fitted

questiontext.text: Read the work-order note again. When may you fit a connector, according to the note?

generalfeedback.text: The note ends with a clear rule: do not fit any connector until the reference is confirmed against the diagram.

answer.text: As soon as the night shift has left

feedback.text: No — the shift ending does not confirm the code.

answer.text: Before you call the OEM support desk

feedback.text: No — you confirm with the OEM first.

answer.text: Once the BITE readout shows any code

feedback.text: No — a code alone is not a confirmed reference.

name.text: U31-U1 Tag — you confirmed the part number

questiontext.text:
Add the correct question tag. Type only the tag, without the question mark.

You confirmed the part number, ____?

generalfeedback.text: Past simple confirmed has no auxiliary, so the tag uses did. Positive statement takes a negative tag: didn’t you.

name.text: U31-U2 Tag — that is not the connector

questiontext.text:
Add the correct question tag. Type only the tag, without the question mark.

That is not the connector, ____?

generalfeedback.text: A negative statement takes a positive tag. Flip the polarity: is not → is it.

name.text: U31-U3 Tag — we can reseat it

questiontext.text:
Add the correct question tag. Type only the tag, without the question mark.

We can reseat the connector, ____?

generalfeedback.text: The modal can comes back in the tag. Positive statement takes a negative tag: can’t we.

name.text: U31-U4 Bank term — say it in your own words

questiontext.text:
Write one word from the vocabulary bank.

To say the same thing in your own words is to ____.

generalfeedback.text: To paraphrase is to say the same thing in your own words — the core check-back move in a lingua franca.

name.text: U31-U5 Bank term — shared language of non-native speakers

questiontext.text:
Write the two-word term from the vocabulary bank.

A shared language between non-native speakers is a ____.

generalfeedback.text: English at the line station is a lingua franca — a shared second language for people whose first languages differ.

name.text: U31-U6 Tag — the readout shows open

questiontext.text:
Make this a confirmation question. Add the correct tag. Type only the tag, without the question mark.

The readout shows “open”, ____?

generalfeedback.text: Present simple shows (third person) has no auxiliary, so the tag uses does: doesn’t it.

name.text: U31-V1 Match the technical term to its meaning

questiontext.text: Match each technical term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: connector = the whole part that joins two wire sets; pin = one contact inside it; BITE = the built-in self-test; readout = the message shown; ambiguous = able to mean two things.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some pairs are right — check the rest.

incorrectfeedback.text: Review the vocabulary bank and try again.

answer.text: a part that joins two sets of electrical wires
a small metal contact inside a connector
the built-in test a system runs on itself
the message or value a system shows you
able to mean two things, so not clear

name.text: U31-V2 Match the strategy verb to its meaning

questiontext.text: Match each communication-strategy verb to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: clarify = make an unclear meaning clear; confirm = make sure it is true or agreed; paraphrase = say it in your own words; read back = repeat it word for word; spell out = say each letter.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some pairs are right — check the rest.

incorrectfeedback.text: These verbs are near-synonyms — review the differences.

answer.text: make sure something is true or agreed
say the same thing in your own words
repeat what you heard, word for word
say each letter, so a word is clear

name.text: U31-V3 Collocation — reseat the ___

questiontext.text:
Complete the collocation. Which word fits?

reseat the ____

generalfeedback.text: We reseat the connector — push it back into place. You do not reseat a readout, a register or a diagram.

feedback.text: No — you check a wiring diagram, not reseat it.

name.text: U31-V4 Collocation — run the ___ test

questiontext.text:
Complete the collocation. Which word fits?

run the ____ test

generalfeedback.text: We run the BITE test — the built-in test the system runs on itself.

feedback.text: No — a reference is a code, not a test.
No — the connector is a part, not a test.
No — the readout is the result the test shows.
